hints: Look at where each wave first returns to zero displacement going downwards on the time axis: wave X completes one full cycle in about half the time taken by wave Y.
Recall that period $T$ is the time for one oscillation and frequency $f = 1/T$, so the wave with the longer $T$ has the smaller $f$.
Compare the maximum vertical heights from the zero line: the crest of wave Y reaches about twice as far as the crest of wave X, and amplitude is that maximum displacement magnitude.
walkthrough: Identify period from the displacement-time graph. For wave X, one full oscillation from $0$ back to the same slope finishes when wave Y has only completed half an oscillation.
Count cycles in the same time interval: wave X completes two full cycles in the time wave Y completes one full cycle, so $T_Y = 2T_X$.
Identify amplitude as the maximum displacement from equilibrium, the height of a crest above the time axis. The crest of wave Y is about twice as tall as the crest of wave X.
With wave X amplitude $A$, wave Y amplitude is $2A$. Frequency $\frac{1}{2}f$ with amplitude $2A$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Frequency $\frac{1}{2}f$ is correct for the longer period, but amplitude $\frac{1}{2}A$ is wrong because the peak displacement of wave Y is larger than that of wave X.

B.explanation: Wave Y has twice the period of wave X so $f_Y = \frac{1}{2}f$, and twice the peak displacement so amplitude $2A$.

C.explanation: Both parts are reversed: wave Y oscillates more slowly so its frequency is less than $f$, and its peaks are taller so its amplitude is greater than $A$.

D.explanation: Amplitude $2A$ is correct for the taller peaks, but frequency $2f$ is wrong because wave Y takes longer than wave X to complete one oscillation.
